summary: A plain nazir shaves on day thirty-one, but if he shaved on day thirty it still counts. If he said "thirty days," shaving on day thirty does not count.

chunks.en: Someone who said, "I am a nazir,"
chunks.st: One who said: I am hereby a nazirite,
chunks.stMore: without specifying how long his term of naziriteship would last,

chunks.en: shaves on day thirty-one.
chunks.st: shaves his hair on the thirty-first day
chunks.stMore: after the start of his naziriteship, as an unspecified term of naziriteship lasts thirty days.

chunks.en: And if he shaved on day thirty, it counts.
chunks.st: And if he shaved on the thirtieth day, he has fulfilled his obligation.

chunks.en: If he said, "I am a nazir for thirty days,"
chunks.st: If he explicitly said: I am hereby a nazirite for thirty days,

chunks.he: אִם גִּלַּח לְיוֹם שְׁלשִׁים לֹא יָצָא:
chunks.en: if he shaved on day thirty, it does not count.
chunks.explain: He said "thirty days," so he must keep thirty full days.
chunks.st: then, if he shaved on the thirtieth day, he has not fulfilled his obligation.
chunks.stMore: Since the naziriteship would have been for thirty days even without him stating: For thirty days, this addition is understood to indicate that he will observe naziriteship for a full thirty days.

summary: Someone who promised two times of nezirus shaves on day 31 and on day 61. The mishnah teaches what happens if he shaved a day early, as Rabbi Papias taught.

chunks.en: Someone who promised two times of nezirus
chunks.st: One who accepted two terms of naziriteship

chunks.he: מְגַלֵּחַ אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה יוֹם שְׁלשִׁים וְאֶחָד,
chunks.en: shaves for the first on day thirty-one,
chunks.st: shaves at the close of the first naziriteship on the thirty-first day,

chunks.en: and for the second on day sixty-one.
chunks.st: and at the close of the second term on the sixty-first day.
chunks.stMore: Since his second term of naziriteship begins after shaving on the thirty-first day, the sixty-first day of the first term is the thirty-first day of his second term.

chunks.he: וְאִם גִּלַּח אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה יוֹם שְׁלשִׁים,
chunks.en: And if he shaved for the first on day thirty,
chunks.st: And if he shaved for the first term on the thirtieth day,

chunks.en: he shaves for the second on day sixty.
chunks.st: he shaves for the second term on the sixtieth day,
chunks.stMore: which is the thirty-first day after the start of his second term of naziriteship.

chunks.he: וְאִם גִּלַּח יוֹם שִׁשִּׁים חָסֵר אֶחָד, יָצָא.
chunks.en: And if he shaved on day sixty less one, it counts.
chunks.st: And if he shaved for the second term on day sixty less one, he has fulfilled his obligation,
chunks.stMore: as this is the thirtieth day of his second term.

chunks.en: Rabbi Papias gave this testimony
chunks.st: And this testimony was attested to by Rabbi Pappeyas, who heard from his teachers

chunks.en: about someone who promised two times of nezirus:
chunks.st: with regard to one who vowed to observe two terms of naziriteship,

chunks.he: שֶׁאִם גִּלַּח אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה שְׁלשִׁים יוֹם,
chunks.en: if he shaved for the first on day thirty,
chunks.st: that if he shaved for the first term on the thirtieth day,

chunks.en: he shaves for the second on day sixty.
chunks.st: he shaves for the second term on the sixtieth day.

chunks.he: וְאִם גִּלַּח לְיוֹם שִׁשִּׁים חָסֵר אֶחָד, יָצָא,
chunks.en: And if he shaved on day sixty less one, it counts,
chunks.st: And if he shaved for the second term on the day sixty less one, he has fulfilled his obligation,

chunks.he: שֶׁיּוֹם שְׁלשִׁים עוֹלֶה לוֹ מִן הַמִּנְיָן:
chunks.en: because day thirty counts for him in the number.
chunks.explain: Day thirty counts for the first and also for the second.
chunks.st: because the thirtieth day of the first term of naziriteship counts as part of his tally of the second term.

summary: If a nazir becomes tamei from a dead person on day thirty, his days are undone and he starts again. Rabbi Eliezer says he loses only seven days.

chunks.en: Someone who said, "I am a nazir,"
chunks.st: One who said: I am hereby a nazirite, without further specification,

chunks.en: and he became tamei on day thirty,
chunks.st: if he became ritually impure through contact with a corpse on the thirtieth day of his term of naziriteship,

chunks.en: it undoes everything.
chunks.explain: He must start his nezirus over again.
chunks.st: it negates the entire tally,
chunks.stMore: and he must start his naziriteship afresh.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: it undoes only seven days.
chunks.st: It negates only seven days,
chunks.stMore: which he must observe until his purification, after which he brings his offerings.

chunks.en: If he said, "I am a nazir for thirty days,"
chunks.st: If he said: I am hereby a nazirite for thirty days,

chunks.en: and he became tamei on day thirty,
chunks.st: and he became impure on the thirtieth day,

chunks.en: it undoes everything.
chunks.st: everyone agrees that it negates the entire tally.

summary: A nazir for a hundred days became tamei at the very end. The first Tanna says he loses all his days, or thirty days. Rabbi Eliezer says he loses only thirty, or only seven.

chunks.en: If he said, "I am a nazir for a hundred days,"
chunks.st: If he said: I am hereby a nazirite for one hundred days,

chunks.en: and he became tamei on day one hundred,
chunks.st: if he became impure on the one hundredth day,

chunks.en: it undoes everything.
chunks.st: it negates the entire tally.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: it undoes only thirty days.
chunks.st: It negates only thirty days,
chunks.stMore: and he observes the final thirty days again.

chunks.en: If he became tamei on day one hundred and one,
chunks.st: If he became impure on the one hundred and first day before bringing his offerings,

chunks.en: it undoes thirty days.
chunks.st: it negates only thirty days, but does not negate all of the observed days.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: it undoes only seven days.
chunks.st: It negates only seven days.

summary: If someone becomes a nazir while in a cemetery, his nezirus does not start yet. If he goes out and comes back in, his days count, and he brings korbanos for becoming tamei.

chunks.en: Someone who became a nazir while he was in a cemetery,
chunks.st: One who took a vow of naziriteship while in a cemetery,

chunks.en: even if he was there thirty days,
chunks.st: even if he was there for a full thirty days without leaving,

chunks.en: those days do not count for him,
chunks.explain: His nezirus has not started yet.
chunks.st: those days he spent in the cemetery do not count as part of his tally,
chunks.stMore: since his naziriteship has not yet gone into effect.

chunks.en: and he does not bring the korban of tumah.
chunks.st: And he therefore does not bring the three offerings of impurity,
chunks.stMore: brought by a nazirite when rendered ritually impure by contact with a corpse, despite having been in a cemetery.

chunks.en: If he went out and came back in,
chunks.st: If he left the cemetery and entered it again,

chunks.en: the days count for him,
chunks.st: those days do count as part of his tally, meaning the naziriteship takes effect,

chunks.en: and he brings the korban of tumah.
chunks.st: and he does bring the offerings of impurity for reentering the cemetery.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: not if he came back on that same day,
chunks.st: This halakha does not apply to one who entered the cemetery on the very day that he left it,

chunks.en: as the Torah says, "And the first days will fall away,"
chunks.st: as it is stated with regard to the halakhot of a ritually impure nazirite: “But the first days shall be void”
chunks.stMore: (Numbers 6:12), which indicates that he does not bring the offerings

chunks.en: until he has some "first days."
chunks.explain: He needs some days of being a tahor nazir first.
chunks.st: until he will have “first days” of purity,
chunks.stMore: during which he observed his naziriteship.

summary: If someone kept his nezirus outside Eretz Yisrael and then came to Eretz Yisrael, Beis Hillel say he must keep it all again. The mishnah tells the story of Queen Helene, who was a nazir for many years.

chunks.en: Someone who promised many days of nezirus
chunks.st: One who vowed many days of naziriteship while outside Eretz Yisrael,

chunks.en: and finished his nezirus,
chunks.st: and completed his naziriteship,

chunks.en: and after that came to Eretz Yisrael:
chunks.st: and afterward came to Eretz Yisrael,
chunks.stMore: in order to bring the offerings at the end of his naziriteship,

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: he is a nazir for thirty days,
chunks.st: He must be a nazirite for thirty days,
chunks.stMore: so that he has observed a term of naziriteship in ritual purity in Eretz Yisrael,

chunks.en: and Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: he is a nazir from the beginning.
chunks.explain: He must keep all his nezirus again.
chunks.st: He is a nazirite from the beginning,
chunks.stMore: that is, he must observe his entire naziriteship again.

chunks.en: There was a story with Queen Helene,
chunks.st: The mishna cites a related story: An incident occurred with regard to Queen Helene,

chunks.en: whose son went to war.
chunks.st: whose son had gone to war,

chunks.he: וְאָמְרָה, אִם יָבֹא בְנִי מִן הַמִּלְחָמָה
chunks.en: She said, "If my son comes back from the war
chunks.st: and she said: If my son will return from war

chunks.en: safely, I will be a nazir for seven years."
chunks.st: safely, I will be a nazirite for seven years.

chunks.en: Her son came back from the war,
chunks.st: And her son returned safely from the war,

chunks.en: and she was a nazir for seven years.
chunks.st: and she was a nazirite for seven years.

chunks.en: At the end of seven years she went up to Eretz Yisrael,
chunks.st: And at the end of seven years, she ascended to Eretz Yisrael,

chunks.en: and Beis Hillel taught her that she must be a nazir
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel instructed her, in accordance with their opinion, that she should be a nazirite

chunks.en: for seven more years.
chunks.st: for an additional seven years.

chunks.en: At the end of those seven years she became tamei,
chunks.explain: So she had to keep seven more years.
chunks.st: And at the end of those seven years she became ritually impure,
chunks.stMore: and was therefore required to observe yet another seven years of naziriteship, as ritual impurity negates the tally of a nazirite.

chunks.en: So she was a nazir for twenty-one years.
chunks.st: And she was found to be a nazirite for twenty-one years.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda said:

chunks.en: She was a nazir only
chunks.st: She was a nazirite for

chunks.en: fourteen years.
chunks.st: only fourteen years and not twenty-one.

summary: Two groups of witnesses disagree: one says he promised two times of nezirus, and one says five. Beis Shammai say there is no nezirus at all. Beis Hillel say he keeps two.

chunks.en: Someone about whom two groups of
chunks.st: In a case of one who had two sets of

chunks.en: witnesses spoke:
chunks.st: witnesses testifying about him
chunks.stMore: that he had taken a vow of naziriteship for a certain period,

chunks.en: these say he promised two,
chunks.st: and these witnesses testify that he took a vow of naziriteship for two terms,

chunks.en: and these say he promised five.
chunks.st: and these witnesses testify that he took a vow of naziriteship for five terms.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: the testimony is split, and there is no nezirus here.
chunks.st: The testimony is divided, i.e., the testimonies contradict each other, and since the testimonies are in conflict they are both rejected entirely and there is no naziriteship here at all.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:
chunks.stMore: The testimonies are not completely in conflict with each other,

chunks.en: two are included in five,
chunks.st: as two terms are included in five terms, and the unanimous testimony,

chunks.en: so he is a nazir two times.
chunks.st: that he is a nazirite for two terms, is accepted.
